source_text:
Ὁ οἰκτίρμων κατὰ πάντα καὶ εὐεργετικὸς πατὴρ ἔχει σπλάγχνα ἐπὶ τοὺς φοβουμένους αὐτόν, ἠπίως τε καὶ προσηνῶς τὰς χάριτας αὐτοῦ ἀποδιδοῖ τοῖς προσερχομένοις αὐτῷ ἁπλῇ διανοιᾳ.
διὸ μὴ διψυχῶμεν, μηδὲ ἰνδαλλέσθω ἡ ψυχὴ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ ταῖς ὑπερβαλλούσαις καὶ ἐνδόξοις δωρεαῖς αὐτοῦ.
πόρρω γενέσθω ἀφ̓ ἡμῶν ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη, ὅπου λέγει: Ταλαίπωροί εἰσιν οἱ δίψυχοι, οἱ διστάζοντες τῇ ψυχῇ, οἱ λέγοντες: Ταῦτα ἠκούσαμεν καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, καὶ ἰδού, γεγηράκαμεν, καὶ οὐδὲν ἡμῖν τούτων συνβέβηκεν.
ὧ ἀνόητοι, συμβάλετε ἑαυτοὺς ξύλῳ: λάβετε ἄμπελον: πρῶτον μὲν φυλλοροεῖ, εἶτα βλαστὸς γίνεται, εἶτα φύλλον, εἶτα ἄνθος, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὄμφαξ, εἶτα σταφυλὴ παρεστηκυῖα. ὁρᾶτε, ὅτι ἐν καιρῷ ὀλίγῳ εἰς πέπειρον καταντᾷ ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ ξύλου.
ἐπ’ ἀληθείας ταχὺ καὶ ἐξαίφνης τελειωθήσεται τὸ βούλημα αὐτοῦ, συνεπιμαρτυρούσης καὶ τῆς γραφῆς, ὅτι ταχὺ ἥξει καὶ οὐ χρονιεῖ, καὶ ἐξαίφνης ἥξει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος, ὃν ὑμεῖς προσδοκᾶτε.
thought_title: The double-minded must not doubt God's swift gifts
orientation: The Roman church continues its appeal, now warning the Corinthians against doubting God's promised gifts by quoting a now-lost scripture about the double-minded and the vine's swift fruit.
pass_a_gloss: The compassionate in all things and beneficent Father has bowels toward those who fear him, and gently and kindly he gives back his graces to those who come to him with a simple mind. Therefore let us not be double-minded, nor let our soul imagine itself upon his surpassing and glorious gifts. Let this scripture be far from us, where it says: Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in the soul, those who say: These things we heard also in the days of our fathers, and behold, we have grown old, and none of these things has happened to us. O foolish ones, compare yourselves to a tree: take a vine: first it puts out leaves, then a shoot comes, then a leaf, then a flower, and after these things a sour grape, then a ripe grape standing by. You see, that in a little time the fruit of the tree arrives at ripeness. In truth quickly and suddenly his will will be brought to completion, the scripture also bearing witness with it, that quickly he will come and will not delay, and suddenly the Lord will come into his temple, and the holy one, whom you await.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Greek word for inward parts, preserving the physical metaphor for compassion that the source uses.
Literal rendering of the compound 'double-souled'; the passage hinges on this term for wavering doubt.
rejected: let us be of two minds

choices.why: Rare verb meaning to appear or imagine oneself; literal rendering keeps the middle voice and the sense of the soul picturing itself upon the gifts.
Specific Greek term for the unripe, sour grape stage before the ripe grape; literal rendering preserves the agricultural sequence.
Perfect participle of 'stand beside'; literal rendering keeps the image of the ripe grape present and ready.
Compound verb meaning to testify jointly; literal rendering preserves the sense that scripture joins in confirming the point.

bible_refs.note: ἐξαίφνης ἥξει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος, ὃν ὑμεῖς προσδοκᾶτε

pass_b_english: The Father is compassionate in every way and rich in good works. He feels tenderly toward those who fear him, and he gently and kindly gives his gifts to those who come to him with a sincere mind.
So let us not be double-minded, and let us not let our souls be deceived by his surpassing and glorious gifts.

Let this Scripture be far from us, where it says: “Wretched are the double-minded, those who doubt in their soul, those who say: ‘We heard these things even in the days of our fathers, and look, we have grown old, and none of these things has happened to us.’”

You fools, compare yourselves to a tree. Take a vine: first it sheds its leaves, then a shoot comes, then a leaf, then a flower, and after these a sour grape, then a ripe grape standing ready. You see that in a short time the fruit of the tree reaches ripeness.

Truly his will will be brought to completion quickly and suddenly, as Scripture also bears witness, that he will come quickly and will not delay, and the Lord will come suddenly to his temple, and the Holy One whom you expect will come.

problems.why: Greek says the vine first puts out leaves, not loses them; opposite action.

problems.quote: let our soul not imagine itself upon his surpassing and glorious gifts
problems.source_quote: μηδὲ ἰνδαλλέσθω ἡ ψυχὴ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ ταῖς ὑπερβαλλούσαις καὶ ἐνδόξοις δωρεαῖς αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Greek says the soul should not be deluded by the gifts, not imagine itself on them.
problems.fix: let our soul not be deluded by his exceeding and glorious gifts

edits.old: let our soul not imagine itself upon his surpassing and glorious gifts
edits.new: let our soul not be deluded by his surpassing and glorious gifts

fixed: The mistranslation of 'μηδὲ ἰνδαλλέσθω ἡ ψυχὴ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ ταῖς ὑπερβαλλούσαις καὶ ἐνδόξοις δωρεαῖς αὐτοῦ' is real; the English now says the soul should not be deluded by the gifts, matching the Greek.

problems.source_quote: the Greek passage gives no biblical citation here
problems.why: The English adds scriptural references that are not present in the source text.
problems.ruling: Source text contains no citation; English adds '(Habakkuk 2:3; Malachi 3:1)' not present in the Greek.

fixed: Removed the parenthetical scriptural citation (Habakkuk 2:3; Malachi 3:1), which is not present in the source text.

problems.quote: the Scripture also bearing witness together with it
problems.why: The phrase 'with it' is vague and the syntax is garbled; it is unclear what 'it' refers to.
problems.fix: Revise to 'as Scripture also bears witness,'

variants.text: the Scripture also bearing witness together with it

edits.old: with the Scripture also bearing witness together with it

problems.quote: and the Holy One whom you expect.
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἐξαίφνης ἥξει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος, ὃν ὑμεῖς προσδοκᾶτε
problems.why: The Holy One shares the verb “will come”; English leaves a fragment and drops that claim.
problems.fix: and suddenly the Lord will come to his temple, and the Holy One whom you expect.
problems.ruling: Source 'ἥξει ὁ κύριος εἰς τὸν ναὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος' makes the Holy One a second subject of 'will come'; English fragment loses that.

edits.old: and the Holy One whom you expect
edits.new: and the Holy One whom you expect will come

fixed: Real omission: source καὶ ὁ άγιος shares ἥξει with ὁ κύριος; added repeated 'will come' — suggested fix still left a fragment.

polish.changed: Clarified who is speaking and acting, made pronoun references explicit, smoothed sentence order for natural modern reading, and kept every claim and quotation intact.

last_rejected.quote: and the Holy One whom you expect.
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ ὁ ἅγιος, ὃν ὑμεῖς προσδοκᾶτε
last_rejected.why: Source has no closing quotation mark; English closes the quote, but the real issue is the phrase is complete and correct. No error found on review.
last_rejected.ruling: English phrase matches Greek καὶ ὁ ἅγιος, ὃν ὑμεῖς προσδοκᾶτε; no omission.

last_rejected.quote: and after these a sour grape, then a ripe grape standing by
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ὄμφαξ, εἶτα σταφυλὴ παρεστηκυῖα
last_rejected.why: ὄμφαξ means ‘bud’, not ‘sour grape’; the translation changes the image of the vine’s growth.
last_rejected.fix: and after these a bud, then a bunch of ripe grapes presented
last_rejected.ruling: ὄμφαξ means unripe/sour grape (LSJ), fitting the vine growth sequence from flower to unripe then ripe grape.

last_rejected.quote: happened to us.’” You fools, compare yourselves to a tree.
last_rejected.source_quote: ὅπου λέγει: Ταλαίπωροί εἰσιν οἱ δίψυχοι… ὧ ἀνόητοι, συμβάλετε ἑαυτοὺς ξύλῳ… ὁ καρπὸς τοῦ ξύλου.
last_rejected.why: The vine parable is still the cited writing. English closes the quote and makes it Clement’s rebuke.
last_rejected.fix: Keep “You fools… reaches ripeness” inside the same Scripture quotation.
last_rejected.ruling: In the Greek, the quotation ends at "συμβέβηκεν". "ὧ ἀνόητοι, συμβάλετε ἑαυτοὺς ξύλῳ" is the author's own address, so closing the quote there is correct.

last_rejected.quote: let us not let our souls be deceived by his surpassing and glorious gifts
last_rejected.source_quote: μηδὲ ἰνδαλλέσθω ἡ ψυχὴ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ ταῖς ὑπερβαλλούσαις καὶ ἐνδόξοις δωρεαῖς αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: The soul must not form fancies about the gifts. The gifts are not said to deceive the soul.
last_rejected.fix: nor let our soul indulge in vain fancies about his surpassing and glorious gifts.
last_rejected.ruling: "ἰνδαλλέσθω … ἐπὶ ταῖς δωρεαῖς" (be led astray or form fancies over the gifts) permits "deceived by". It is loose but within range and does not reverse the meaning.
